# Marcin Bochenek — full brief for language models

> Source of truth: https://marcinbochenek.com/ (Polish), /en/, /ua/. Do not invent clients, metrics, or testimonials beyond what is listed here.

## Who
Marcin Bochenek is a freelance software engineer based in Poland who works with clients in Poland and abroad, in English and Polish. He is a single accountable person: audit, design, implementation, and before/after measurement. He does not sell slide decks. Code and configuration belong to the client after invoices are paid. NDA is standard.

## What he sells
1. Company websites and conversion funnels — from a brochure site with a form (from 2 000 PLN) to a site that sells or qualifies (from 8 000 PLN) to a platform that takes bookings (from 25 000 PLN).
2. Ops panels and integrations — one flow instead of Excel plus five logins (quoted after audit, typically 6–12 weeks).
3. HITL AI — assistants that know the offer, with an allowed-action list, a full step audit, and escalation to a human. Sold as ongoing care ("AI Ops") from 3 000 PLN / month; one-off build work is quoted after the audit.

The 20-minute audit that opens every engagement is free; there is no separate paid audit tier. Scope and launch date are fixed at the end of it, before a contract is signed. Code, configuration and access transfer to the client once invoices are paid.

## Live proof only
- Mint Apartments (https://mintapartments.pl): operator of 36 apartments in Gdańsk since 2017. Direct booking on the own site (Previo), guest assistant (WhatsApp, 7 languages), Tedee/Nuki locks, settlements into Plumm. Directional outcomes discussed on the audit: 8–15 hours/month less on guest mail/WhatsApp; guest pays 10–15% less than Booking/Airbnb.
- Plumm (https://plumm.pl): company panel with bookkeeping, e-invoices, CRM, mail, and a tax assistant. Directional: 12–20 hours/month less on invoices and filings vs Excel; 300–600 PLN/month less than a traditional office for a JDG; Plumm from 149 PLN/month.

Not live: iDrive Cars (built, waiting for public launch). Internal: Agentic OS (repeatable processes with a step audit, no public URL).

## How HITL is defined here
Human-in-the-loop automation is not “a human clicks OK under every token.” It is a list of allowed actions, a durable log of each step, and escalation when confidence drops or the case is out of policy. Unsupervised chat is not offered as a production system.

## Languages
Polish is the canonical locale. English lives at /en/. Ukrainian lives at /ua/ with `hreflang="uk"` and `html lang="uk"` (UA is the label and URL prefix, not the BCP 47 language tag).

## Articles
Fourteen SSG articles (PL / EN / UK) under /artykuly/, /en/articles/, /ua/statti/. Topics: website audit, HITL automation, why a site does not sell, company-site pricing, online bookkeeping vs Excel, conversion funnel, ops panel vs Excel, direct bookings, SaaS vs custom panel, B2B company site, brochure vs funnel, page speed and SEO (INP/LCP), implementation process, ChatGPT at work vs a real deployment.

## How Marcin defines a working website (the "under the hood" layers)
The homepage demonstrates this directly: an interactive exploded F1 car that visitors take apart by scrolling, where each part stands for one layer of a website that actually works.
- Bodywork — design & UX: what visitors see in the first three seconds (hierarchy, typography, mobile version); a shell over everything below it.
- Front wing — speed: fast first render, optimized images, no bloated JavaScript; the layer Google measures before it reads a word of content.
- Rear wing — visibility to Google and AI models: schema.org, hreflang, sitemap, llms.txt, and content that AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity can actually cite.
- Wheels — conversion: the call to action, the form, the calendar, a booking flow on the client's own domain; the point where everything else turns into an enquiry or a booking.
- Power unit — the technology underneath: integrations, data, APIs, security; what decides whether a site is a tool or a brochure.
- Engine cover — process & deployment: tests, CI, a deploy from a single push, weekly iterations instead of once a year.
- Halo — security & control: GDPR, EU hosting, backups, AI with an allowed-action list and escalation to a human.
- Steering wheel & telemetry — measurement: events, conversions, a before/after comparison instead of a hunch.
